class.name: Wheel
class.brief_description: A vehicle wheel with suspension raycasting and tire-force simulation.
class.description: Wheel is a [Node3D] child of an [Axle]. Vehicle setup requires exactly two distinct wheels per axle. The wheel owns suspension contact state, tire forces, rotation, and an internally created raycast/skid-mark helper. After relaxation and combined-grip limiting, a grounded solve submits contact geometry, slip velocities, final tire forces, and normal load to that helper. This does not change tire-force or traction-control behavior. Only the bound read-only accessors below are part of the Godot API.

method.name: get_angular_velocity
method.description: Returns wheel angular velocity in radians per second.

method.name: get_tire_force
method.description: Returns the latest world-space tire force vector.

method.name: get_collision_point
method.description: Returns the latest world-space ground contact point.

method.name: get_collision_normal
method.description: Returns the latest world-space ground contact normal.

method.name: is_on_ground
method.description: Returns whether the suspension raycast currently contacts a surface.

method.name: get_slip_ratio
method.description: Returns the instantaneous longitudinal slip ratio: (wheel tread speed - contact forward speed) / sqrt(contact forward speed squared + 9). The smooth 3 m/s regularization keeps the ratio finite near rest. This same normalization is used for longitudinal tire force and ABS.

method.name: get_slip_angle
method.description: Returns the current lateral slip angle in degrees.

method.name: get_is_sliding
method.description: Returns whether longitudinal or lateral slip currently exceeds the tire sliding threshold.

method.name: get_abs_active
method.description: Returns whether ABS is currently reducing brake pressure for this wheel.

method.name: set_grip_multiplier
method.description: Sets the runtime multiplier applied to both longitudinal and lateral tire grip.

members.member: Runtime multiplier for authored longitudinal and lateral grip. Use 1.0 for authored grip, 0.0 for no tire force, and values above 1.0 for additional grip.
